newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WARNE TAKES CAREER BEST TO ROUT WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE TAKES CAREER BEST TO ROUT WEST INDIES.

text.p: Australia leg-spinner Shane Warne claimed five wickets in 15 deliveries in his best performance in a limited overs international to send West Indies crashing to an eight-wicket defeat on Sunday.
Brian Lara added to West Indies' woes with another batting failure on a dismal day for the tourists after their collapse in the World Series competition at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
In reply to West Indies' disappointing 161 all out in 48.3 overs, Australia cruised to 162 for two with exactly eight overs to spare.

Australia opener Mark Waugh steered the hosts home with a perfectly paced 83 not out in 134 balls, including five fours. Warne brought about a dramatic end to the West Indies innings by taking their last five wickets to fall at a cost of just four runs to the bowler.
The Victoria captain was twice denied a hat-trick as he hastened West Indies to their demise on a slow wicket of variable bounce.
Warne's match figures of five for 33 in 9.3 overs in his 61st international ecplised his previous best of four for 19 against New Zealand three years ago.
Lara managed to avoid being one of Warne's victims but his score of 26 in 48 balls took his tally of runs in his last four innings to a meagre 34.
West Indies, beaten by five wickets against Australia in the opening match of the competition on Friday, lost their last six wickets for 19 runs in the space of 37 deliveries.

Warne dismissed middle order batsman Roland Holder and fast bowler Nixon McLean in successive deliveries and then repeated the feat in his next over to remove wicketkeeper Junior Murray and pace bowler Kenneth Benjamin.
